notes: The page is a typescript continuation comprising two paragraphs and 26 base lines, with two typed interlinear insertions, five cancellation groups (one continuing across L11–12), a short underline beneath R, and pencil archive number 37. There are no diagrams, drawings, displays, title, dateline, signature, or authorial page number. Example 3 is a reference, not a page count.

The first paragraph describes coverings through local finite-set inertia actions and matching compatibility, states an analogous description for Galois coverings using commuting left G_i and right H actions on H-torsors, gives Hom(G_i,H)/H, and claims an étale-local reduction for a full-faithfulness criterion. These are document claims; the surrounding geometric criterion is not independently verified here.

The second paragraph agrees with an interpretation of the Kummer example and says the intended order is divisibility. The n-prime/n interval is visibly empty; no order relation is supplied from this prose.

Exact unusual forms kept include makes a sense, stricly, convevient, and the explicit mixed-letter readings in rahher/rather, pocal/local, mihd/mind, the second realization, and the first two cells of sormulation/formulation. No correction chronology is assigned to mixed typewriter cells.

The first insertion is placed after E.; the second after means, according to immediate spatial starts. No caret or arrow occurs. The comma after arbitrary is included in its insertion; no comma is visible after the second insertion.
The lower G-mark is detached and curved; the conventional cedilla/breve encoding approximates shape without asserting intentional accents. It remains explicitly uncertain.
The mixed G/H group capital was inspected independently of the later plain H actions. The later H notation did not determine the earlier glyph. No mathematical expectation changed an ink reading.

All math in the text was inspected, including the dotted lower i on Z_i and G_i, all S-primes, the three H letters in Hom(G_i,H)/H (including Hom initial), the quotient slash, the underlined plain R, and the raised prime on n. The insertions, deletions, quotation marks and literal hyphen spacing were compared with both witnesses.

The whole and each half were displayed once. Fifteen crops were created and displayed once each, without OCR, recognition, internet, or other-page images. No other reader content was opened. Only assigned output paths were written. C_prior_questions and notation_snapshot were treated as questions/provisional guidance, not authority over the scan.

checks.statement: For a finite group H and a group A, nonempty finite right H-torsors equipped with a commuting left A-action are classified up to equivariant isomorphism by Hom(A,H)/H.
checks.outcome: Verified in this run for the stated finite-H refinement: choose e in E and define rho(a) by a.e=e.rho(a). Commutation gives rho(ab)=rho(a)rho(b). Replacing e by e.h conjugates rho by h^{-1}; conversely rho defines a.e=rho(a)e on E=H. The free transitive right action makes the reconstruction bijective on equivariant isomorphism classes. This does not check the preceding geometric category equivalence, the full-faithfulness criterion, or a claim with infinite H and finite E.
